faqs.q: What should I include on a plumbing invoice?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name and license number, the client and job-site address, a dated line-item list of services (call-out fee, labor, parts), tax, and a total due. Most states require a contractor license number on client-facing invoices.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate tax automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantity and rate per line, and the subtotal, tax and total update automatically. Leave the tax rate blank if you are not required to charge sales tax.

faqs.q: Where can I find a plumbing invoice sample?
faqs.a: This template is a ready-to-use plumbing invoice sample - it comes pre-filled with common plumbing line items (service call, drain cleaning, faucet install, pipe repair, water heater) at typical rates. Download the Excel version to see the auto-calculating subtotal, tax, and total, then replace the sample items with your own.

deepDive.heading: Plumbing invoicing: T&M vs flat rate, permit costs and the parts markup nobody explains
deepDive.sub: Plumbing is the trade where the customer is most likely to question the bill, because they cannot see what you did inside the wall. These are the conventions that make a plumbing invoice defensible.

blocks.h3: Time and materials or flat rate — the invoice has to match the contract
paras: Residential service work is increasingly sold flat rate: a published price for a job, agreed before the technician starts. Commercial and remodel work is usually time and materials. The two produce different invoices, and mixing them is where disputes start.

Flat-rate invoices show the job description and the price, and nothing about hours — that is the whole point, the customer buys an outcome. T&M invoices must show arrival and departure times, labour hours at the stated rate, and every part with its price. If you sell flat rate but invoice by hours, you have taught the customer to distrust the number. Pick the model per job and say which one on the invoice header.

rows: Must be agreed before work starts
Credit policy must be on the invoice

blocks.h3: Permits, inspections and the work that is not visible
paras: Repiping, water heater replacement, sewer line work and any gas line alteration require a permit in most jurisdictions, and the permit has a cost plus an inspection that occupies a day. Customers routinely assume the plumber absorbs this. Put the permit on the invoice as its own line with the permit number.

The other invisible work is the reason plumbing bills look high: cutting and patching drywall, moving stored items to reach a cleanout, digging to expose a buried line, and the time spent draining and refilling a system. None of it is glamorous, all of it is billable. Itemize access and restoration separately from the plumbing work itself so the customer can see they are paying for two different trades.
steps: Confirm whether the scope needs a permit — repipe, water heater, sewer line and any gas alteration usually do.
Pull the permit before work starts and record the number on the work order.
Schedule the rough inspection if the work will be covered (walls closed, trench backfilled).
Attend the final inspection and attach the signed-off card to the job file.
Bill the permit fee and the inspection time as separate lines on the invoice.

blocks.h3: Parts markup is legitimate — hiding it is not
paras: Plumbing parts are marked up. A supply house sells a ball valve at a trade price; the invoice price reflects the trade price plus handling, stocking, warranty risk and the trip to the truck. Markups of 25 to 100 percent on small parts are standard in service work, and customers who find out later feel cheated only if they feel it was concealed.

The invoice convention that avoids this is to list the part by name and description with a single price — not to print the supply-house cost and a separate markup. Markup on materials is normal business, explained in the terms section once. What is not normal is a line called "misc. parts" for $240, which tells the customer nothing and justifies nothing.
list: List parts with manufacturer and model — not "parts"
One price per part, markup included, no cost column
Warranty on parts vs labour stated separately (parts often 1 year, labour 90 days)
Customer-supplied fixtures: state that warranty covers installation only

blocks.h3: Water heaters, sewer lines and the big-ticket jobs
paras: A water heater replacement is a package: unit, expansion tank, pan and drain, venting, gas or electrical connection, permit, haul-away, and typically a six-year tank warranty. Itemize the package rather than quoting a single number, because a competing bid will differ on exactly those items and the customer needs to compare like with like.

Sewer and drain work is priced by the foot once the camera has been run, which is why the camera inspection is a billable line and not a free service. If the line needs excavation, the quote should state the footage, the depth, the restoration and whether the street or the yard is being opened. Those four numbers decide whether the job is $2,000 or $12,000, and a lump sum hides all of them.
list: Water heater: unit, expansion tank, pan/drain, venting, connection, permit, haul-away
Camera inspection: billable, with footage documented on the invoice
Sewer replacement: footage, depth, excavation, restoration named separately
Financing or deposit terms for jobs above a stated threshold

blocks.h3: If your techs still write paper tickets
paras: Many service plumbers still hand-write a ticket on site and the office types the invoice. Print this template on two-part carbonless paper rather than buying pre-printed books: white copy to the customer, yellow to the office. The customer's signature on that ticket is the single best defence against a chargeback.

What a plumbing ticket must record that a generic invoice does not: the fixture or appliance serviced with make and model, the readings taken (water pressure, temperature, flow), what was found on camera, and the parts left on site. A ticket that says "fixed leak" cannot support a $480 bill three weeks later.
list: Readings: static pressure, water temperature, GPM where relevant
Parts installed with model numbers; parts supplied by customer noted separately
Customer signature and date on both copies
